name: solar-system
inputText:
Mercury — smallest planet, closest to the Sun, covered in craters, no atmosphere, extreme temperatures
Venus — second planet, hottest in the solar system, thick toxic clouds, spins backwards, similar size to Earth
Mars — the Red Planet, home to Olympus Mons (tallest volcano), thin atmosphere, has polar ice caps
Jupiter — largest planet, Great Red Spot storm, 79+ moons, made of gas, could fit 1,300 Earths inside
Saturn — famous for its rings made of ice and rock, second largest planet, least dense (would float in water)
Neptune — farthest planet, deep blue color, strongest winds in the solar system (1,200 mph), has 14 moons

rooms.name: Crater Field Furnace
rooms.itemToRemember: Mercury — smallest planet, closest to the Sun, covered in craters, no atmosphere, extreme temperatures
rooms.mnemonic: A tiny silver planet covered in holes like Swiss cheese sits so close to the Sun that one side glows red-hot while the other freezes — no air to spread the heat around.
rooms.sceneDescription: The surface of planet Mercury dominates the frame — a vast cratered landscape stretching to the horizon, with craters of every size pockmarking the gray rocky terrain. The Sun looms enormous in the black sky, three times larger than seen from Earth, blazing with intense white-gold light. The sunlit side of the surface glows orange-hot while shadows in the craters are pitch black. No atmosphere, no clouds — just sharp stars visible in the jet-black sky alongside the giant Sun. A small thermometer graphic embedded in the rocky surface shows extreme heat. The planet's surface is detailed and photorealistic — gray, pitted, barren. Ultra-wide cinematic composition, dramatic lighting contrast.

odysseyKeyframes.prompt: Surface of Mercury — vast cratered gray landscape stretching to horizon. Enormous Sun looms in black sky, three times normal size. Sunlit craters glow orange-hot, shadows pitch black. No atmosphere, stars visible. Photorealistic, ultra-wide cinematic.

Camera moves across Mercury's surface. A meteorite slams into the ground, creating a fresh crater with a flash of light and spray of gray dust. The enormous Sun blazes overhead. Impact debris flies upward in the vacuum and falls back slowly.

The camera pans to the terminator line where Mercury's sunlit side meets the dark side. Dramatic contrast — glowing orange rock transitions sharply to frozen black shadow. The giant Sun sits on the horizon, half-visible. Stars glitter in the black sky above.

rooms.name: Toxic Cloud Oven
rooms.itemToRemember: Venus — second planet, hottest in the solar system, thick toxic clouds, spins backwards, similar size to Earth
rooms.mnemonic: A planet wrapped in thick yellow poisonous blankets like a fever patient — it's the hottest planet because the blankets trap all the heat, and it spins the wrong way like a confused top.
rooms.sceneDescription: Planet Venus seen from just above its thick cloud layer — swirling bands of dense yellow-orange toxic clouds fill the frame, with lightning bolts crackling between cloud layers. The clouds are sulfuric acid, rendered with oily, toxic-looking textures in yellows, oranges, and browns. Below the clouds, the surface glows a hellish orange-red from extreme heat (900°F), visible through gaps in the cloud cover. Volcanic mountains are dimly visible on the surface through the haze. The planet's curvature is visible at the edges. Everything feels oppressively hot and hostile. Photorealistic, dramatic lighting from the glowing surface below, cinematic wide-angle.

odysseyKeyframes.prompt: Venus from above its cloud layer — swirling dense yellow-orange toxic clouds filling the frame. Lightning crackling between layers. Surface glows hellish orange through gaps. Volcanic mountains dimly visible. Planet curvature at edges. Photorealistic, cinematic.

A massive lightning bolt arcs across Venus's cloud layer, illuminating the swirling yellow-brown sulfuric acid clouds from within. The clouds roil and churn violently. The glow from the superheated surface below pulses through gaps in the atmosphere.

The camera descends through a gap in Venus's clouds toward the surface. The hellish orange-red glow intensifies. A massive shield volcano comes into view, lava flowing down its flanks. The thick atmosphere distorts everything with heat shimmer. Unbearably hot and hostile.

rooms.name: Red Dust Volcano
rooms.itemToRemember: Mars — the Red Planet, home to Olympus Mons (tallest volcano), thin atmosphere, has polar ice caps
rooms.mnemonic: A rusty red desert planet with a volcano so tall it pokes through the thin wispy atmosphere into space — and white ice cream scoops sit on its north and south poles.
rooms.sceneDescription: The Martian landscape stretches out in vivid rusty-red desert terrain with Olympus Mons — an enormous shield volcano — rising massively in the background, its peak disappearing into the thin pinkish sky. The volcano is so tall it dwarfs everything, with caldera visible at the summit. Red dust covers everything. The thin Martian atmosphere creates a pale salmon-pink sky with wispy clouds. In the foreground, rust-colored rocky terrain with wind-carved formations. A white polar ice cap gleams on the distant horizon. Two small moons (Phobos and Deimos) are faintly visible in the sky. Photorealistic, epic scale, cinematic wide-angle.

odysseyKeyframes.prompt: Martian landscape — vivid rusty-red desert terrain. Enormous Olympus Mons volcano rises in background, peak disappearing into thin pink sky. Red dust everywhere. Wispy clouds, pale salmon sky. White polar ice cap on horizon. Two small moons visible. Photorealistic, epic cinematic.

A massive Martian dust devil forms in the red desert, spinning red dust hundreds of feet into the thin pink sky. Olympus Mons looms in the background. The swirling column of rust-colored dust catches the sunlight, glowing orange.

The camera rises to show the full scale of Olympus Mons from a distance — the volcano is impossibly huge, its base stretching beyond the horizon, its caldera visible from above. The thin Martian atmosphere fades to black at the edges. The white polar ice cap gleams in the distance.

rooms.name: Storm Eye Arena
rooms.itemToRemember: Jupiter — largest planet, Great Red Spot storm, 79+ moons, made of gas, could fit 1,300 Earths inside
rooms.mnemonic: A gas giant so enormous that 1,300 Earths could fit inside like marbles in a beach ball — with a hurricane eye bigger than Earth that's been raging for centuries.
rooms.sceneDescription: Jupiter's Great Red Spot dominates the frame — an enormous swirling storm system in vivid oranges, reds, and creamy whites, bigger than planet Earth. The iconic bands of Jupiter's atmosphere surround it — alternating stripes of orange, brown, cream, and white swirling gas clouds with incredible turbulent detail. Several of Jupiter's moons are visible as small spheres nearby — one showing ice-cracked Europa, another showing volcanic Io with orange lava spots. The scale is overwhelming. The gas clouds show incredible depth and complexity, with smaller storms and eddies spiraling around the Great Red Spot. Photorealistic, hyper-detailed atmosphere, dramatic lighting, cinematic.

odysseyKeyframes.prompt: Jupiter's Great Red Spot — enormous swirling storm in vivid orange and red, bigger than Earth. Bands of orange, brown, cream gas clouds with turbulent detail. Moons visible — icy Europa, volcanic Io. Overwhelming scale. Photorealistic, hyper-detailed, cinematic.

The Great Red Spot churns and rotates, its swirling orange-red clouds spinning faster. Smaller white storms get pulled into its vortex. Jupiter's atmospheric bands flow in opposite directions, creating shearing turbulence at their boundaries. Lightning flashes deep within the gas layers.

Camera pulls back to reveal Jupiter's full massive sphere — the Great Red Spot now visible as one feature among many. The planet's enormous size dwarfs its visible moons. Colorful atmospheric bands wrap around the entire planet. The gas giant's scale is awe-inspiring and overwhelming.

rooms.name: Ice Ring Gallery
rooms.itemToRemember: Saturn — famous for its rings made of ice and rock, second largest planet, least dense (would float in water)
rooms.mnemonic: A golden planet wearing a spectacular hula-hoop made of billions of ice cubes and pebbles — so light and fluffy that if you could find a big enough bathtub, it would float!
rooms.sceneDescription: Saturn and its magnificent ring system fill the frame in stunning detail. The rings are shown edge-on at a dramatic angle, revealing thousands of individual ringlets made of glittering ice particles and rocky debris — some rings bright white, others translucent, with visible gaps including the dark Cassini Division. Saturn itself is a beautiful pale gold sphere with subtle cream and honey-colored atmospheric bands. Sunlight catches the ice particles in the rings, making them sparkle and shimmer. The planet casts a dark shadow across the far side of the rings. Several small moons are visible between ring gaps. Deep space background with stars. Photorealistic, breathtaking, ultra-wide cinematic composition.

odysseyKeyframes.prompt: Saturn and its magnificent rings fill the frame. Rings at dramatic angle showing thousands of glittering ice ringlets with gaps including Cassini Division. Pale gold planet with cream atmospheric bands. Sunlight makes ice sparkle. Planet shadow on rings. Stars behind. Photorealistic, ultra-wide cinematic.

Camera moves closer to Saturn's rings, revealing the incredible detail — billions of ice chunks and rocky particles orbiting in formation. Sunlight refracts through translucent ice particles creating prismatic rainbow effects. The dark Cassini Division gap separates the bright rings.

Camera sweeps along Saturn's ring plane at ring level, particles of ice and rock streaming past in a cosmic river. Saturn's golden sphere dominates the background. A small shepherd moon carves a clean gap through the ring material. Ice particles glitter like diamonds in sunlight.

rooms.name: Deep Blue Tempest
rooms.itemToRemember: Neptune — farthest planet, deep blue color, strongest winds in the solar system (1,200 mph), has 14 moons
rooms.mnemonic: The farthest planet is a deep blue marble being blasted by supersonic winds so powerful they'd flatten anything on Earth — 1,200 mph hurricanes on a lonely blue world with 14 tiny moon friends.
rooms.sceneDescription: Neptune fills the frame — a stunning deep azure-blue sphere with vivid bands of electric blue, cobalt, and dark navy. Bright white streaks of methane ice clouds race across the surface at incredible speed, stretched into long wisps by the 1,200 mph winds. A dark storm spot similar to Jupiter's but deep blue-black is visible on the surface. Triton, Neptune's largest moon, is visible nearby — a pinkish-white sphere with geysers of nitrogen erupting from its surface. The planet's deep blue color is rich and saturated, almost luminous against the black of deep space. Faint rings are barely visible. Very distant dim Sun provides cold blue lighting. Photorealistic, vivid blues, cinematic composition.

odysseyKeyframes.prompt: Neptune fills the frame — stunning deep azure-blue sphere with electric blue and navy bands. White methane ice clouds streak across at incredible speed. Dark storm spot visible. Triton moon nearby with nitrogen geysers. Luminous blue against black space. Photorealistic, vivid, cinematic.

Neptune's supersonic winds visibly push white cloud bands across the blue surface at tremendous speed. The white methane clouds stretch into long streaks and then dissipate, replaced by new ones. The dark storm spot rotates slowly. Wind shear creates dramatic turbulence patterns.

Camera approaches Neptune's cloud tops. The deep blue atmosphere reveals incredible depth — layers of cobalt, navy, and electric blue. White cloud formations race past the camera at supersonic speed. The blue is mesmerizing and deep, like looking into an infinite ocean. Faint ring material glints in dim sunlight.
